MFL S.Karuppaiah Manager Marketing Organizes Kisan Sangoshthi cum PM PRANAM Awareness Programme at Miryalaguda
articles.full_content:
Madras Fertilizers Limited, Regional Office Hyderabad, organized a Kisan Sangoshthi cum PM PRANAM Awareness Programme today at M/s Veeramanikanta Fertilizer Pesticides, Chinthapalli Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, Nalgonda District.
The programme was organized by Shri S. KARUPPAIAH, Manager (Marketing), Telangana State.
More than 37 progressive farmers from Chinthapalli and surrounding villages participated in the programme. MFL Handouts, Main Banner and Vijay Standy were prominently displayed at the venue and handouts on balanced fertilization were distributed to all farmers.
Shri S. Karuppaiah briefed the farmers about the present dry spell situation in Miryalaguda area and explained in detail the objective of Hon'ble Prime Minister's PM PRANAM Scheme to save Mother Earth by reducing chemical fertilizer load. He also stressed the importance of organic manure, green manure, vermi compost and balanced use of fertilizers for sustainable soil health and better yield. Farmers were advised to avoid indiscriminate use of Urea and DAP.
Farmers actively participated in the interactive session and requested MFL to make Vijay 17-17-17 Complex Fertilizer available immediately in Miryalaguda market. They informed that due to non-availability of Vijay, SPIC 17-17-17 is being sold and they are willing to purchase only Vijay Complex if supplied in time.
Though there was a slight language barrier in explaining technical points in fluent Telugu, the session was managed successfully and all farmers' queries were clarified to their satisfaction.
Good arrangements were done by MFL with the help of Field Assistant. Shamiyana, chairs and public address system were arranged neatly. Biscuits, water bottles, coffee and snacks were provided to all participating farmers.
The programme concluded successfully with full cooperation of the dealer and farmers.
articles.summary: Madras Fertilizers Limited, Regional Office Hyderabad, organized a Kisan Sangoshthi cum PM PRANAM Awareness Programme today at M/s Veeramanikanta Fertilizer Pesticides, Chinthapalli Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, Nalgonda District. More than 37 progressive farmers from Chinthapalli and surrounding villages participated in the programme. MFL Handouts, Main Banner and Vijay Standy were prominently displayed at the venue and handouts on balanced fertilization were distributed to all farmers.

Mumbai, 27 August 2026
Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education, Consumer Affairs and Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, addressed a high-level gathering of investors, developers, financial institutions and industry leaders and stakeholders today at the Mumbai Roadshow for the upcoming Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026.
Delivering the keynote address on the occasion, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Shri Pralhad Joshi urged stakeholders across the energy sector to participate in the upcoming BRESE 2026 , noting that the Summit is generating considerable interest internationally. BRESE 2026 will bring together three major global platforms under one roof — the BRE Summit & Expo, the 9th General Assembly of the International Solar Alliance, and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen. The four-day event is expected to bring together Heads of Government and Energy Ministers from more than 75 countries, global institutional investors, technology providers and over 25,000 participants from across the renewable-energy value chain, Shri Joshi said.
Shri Joshi said that the Summit will provide industry stakeholders an opportunity to build partnerships, explore new markets and engage with global investors and technology providers. For States, the Summit will offer a platform to showcase their project pipelines to global developers and international financial institutions, while for banks and investors, it will facilitate greater convergence between projects and financing opportunities, he added.
Highlighting the growth of the renewable-energy sector in the country, Shri Pralhad Joshi said that India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil-fuel capacity, reaching around 302–303 GW, while the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has reached approximately 53.5 lakh beneficiary households. Shri Joshi also said that India’s non-fossil-fuel capacity has increased from 80.3 GW to 300.5 GW over the last 12 years, registering a 275 per cent increase. During the same period, solar capacity increased from 2.8 GW to 165 GW, representing nearly 5 8-fold growth, while wind capacity rose from around 21 GW to 58 GW, registering a 176 per cent increase. The Union Minister said that India added more than 17 GW of renewable-energy capacity during the first four months of FY 2026–27, including 14.33 GW of solar capacity and over 2 GW of wind capacity.

Kisan Credit Card Saturation Drive to Cover Around 6,000 Bank Branches in West Bengal
articles.full_content:
Mission-mode campaign from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027 to expand institutional credit access for eligible farmers
Kolkata; August 27, 2026
A Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Saturation Drive will be undertaken across West Bengal from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027 to ensure wider coverage of eligible farmers under the institutional agricultural credit framework.
The five-month campaign will involve around 6,000 rural and semi-urban bank branches across the State. The drive will focus on identifying eligible farmers who do not presently have a KCC, facilitating new applications, and undertaking renewal or enhancement of existing KCC limits, wherever required.
Special emphasis will be placed on small and marginal farmers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers and farmers engaged in dairy, fisheries, animal husbandry and other allied activities, besides other eligible categories. Banks will undertake beneficiary identification, awareness generation and application facilitation through branch-level and local outreach activities.
The campaign will be implemented through coordinated efforts of banks, the State Level Bankers’ Committee, State Government departments, district administrations, NABARD and other stakeholders, with monitoring at branch, district and State levels.
The KCC provides timely institutional credit for crop cultivation and eligible allied activities. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, the KCC crop-loan limit has been enhanced to Rs. 5 lakh, while the collateral-free agricultural credit limit has been increased to Rs. 2 lakh per borrower, effective from 1 January 2025.
For eligible KCC crop loans up to Rs. 3 lakh, credit is available at 7 per cent per annum, with an additional 3 per cent interest subvention for eligible farmers making prompt repayment, subject to applicable guidelines.
Digital initiatives such as Kisan Rin Portal, Jan Samarth, e-KCC and KRISHIKA are also supporting streamlined agricultural credit delivery.
The Saturation Drive is aimed at strengthening last-mile delivery of institutional agricultural credit and advancing the objective of “Saturation of Eligible Farmers with Institutional Credit”, thereby supporting agricultural and allied activities, rural livelihoods and financial inclusion across West Bengal.

POWERGRID Facilitates Skill Development and Employment Opportunities for Youth Through SDC Malda
articles.full_content:
Kolkata; August 27, 2026
Continuing its commitment to skill development and sustainable livelihood generation, Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID), under its Corporate Social Responsibility initiative, facilitated the successful completion of training for 54 candidates of the 7th Batch at the Skill Development Centre (SDC), Malda. The programme was attended by Shri Adish Kumar Gupta, Executive Director, Shri Arun Kumar Singh, Chief General Manager (AM), and Shri Sandeep Kumar Barik, Head of Personnel, ER-II, along with other senior officials and stakeholders.
Addressing the gathering, the dignitaries emphasized the importance of skill development in enhancing employability and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for the youth. They appreciated the efforts of the trainees and encouraged them to contribute meaningfully to the nation’s growing power and infrastructure sectors.
Since its inception, the Skill Development Centre at Malda has successfully trained 330 candidates up to the 7th batch. A total of 165 trainees, including 29 from the 7th Batch, have already been placed in leading organizations in the power, transmission, manufacturing, and infrastructure sectors, such as Skipper Limited, Transformers & Reactors (India) Pvt. Ltd., KEC International, Modina International India, JSL, Resonia, Suzlon, and other reputed companies.
A key highlight of the ceremony was the distribution of course completion certificates and job appointment letters to successful trainees by the senior dignitaries. The event marked a significant milestone in the professional journey of the candidates, many of whom have already commenced or are set to commence their careers in leading organizations. The Skill Development Programme has been designed to support youth from the region by providing industry-relevant training along with comprehensive support facilities.
The initiative reflects POWERGRID’s continued commitment towards skill development, youth empowerment, and sustainable community development through meaningful CSR interventions. By bridging the gap between skills and employment, the programme is contributing to the creation of a skilled workforce for the nation’s rapidly expanding power and infrastructure sectors.

National Seminar on Export Promotion and E-Commerce 2026 held at Rangpo, Pakyong
articles.full_content:
Gangtok, 27th August 2026
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), through MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Gangtok, in association with Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and other stakeholders, organised the National Seminar on Export Promotion and E-Commerce 2026 at Rangpo, Pakyong, today.
The seminar aimed at creating awareness among MSMEs of Sikkim on export opportunities, e-commerce platforms, market linkages and institutional support for taking local products to national and international markets.
Ms. Pari Bishnoi, IAS, District Collector, Pakyong, Chief Guest on the occasion, highlighted the need to strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem in the district and enable local entrepreneurs and artisans to access wider markets, especially through e-commerce and exports. She noted the potential of Sikkim’s local and traditional products.
Shri Nirmal Chowdhury, Assistant Director and Head of Office, MSME-DFO, Gangtok, outlined the objective of the seminar and stressed coordinated institutional efforts to help MSMEs understand export procedures and digital commerce. Shri Manoj Singh, Assistant DGFT, Kolkata, spoke on export facilitation, procedures and compliance requirements. Shri Kesang Namthak Tenzing, Regional PF Commissioner, Gangtok, emphasised formalisation and compliance as enterprises grow. Shri Padam Prasad Sharma, Chairman, Farmers Welfare Board, Sikkim, underlined stronger market linkages and value addition for agricultural products.
Shri Akshay Murkute, Assistant Director (Gr-I), MSME-DFO, Gangtok, proposed the Vote of Thanks in the inaugural session.
In the technical session, Dr. Saju Adhikary, Business Development Manager, APEDA, spoke on APEDA’s role in export facilitation for agri and processed food products. Shri P. T. Lepcha, Deputy Director In-Charge, Spices Board, Gangtok, highlighted export promotion initiatives of the Spices Board and opportunities for growers and processors with focus on quality and standards. Shri Sameer Pradha, Marketing Executive, India Post, presented on Dak Ghar Niryat Kendra (DNK) – from Sikkim to World, explaining how the postal network can facilitate exports for small entrepreneurs.
On e-commerce, Shri Anish Pradhan, Senior Manager, Government Affairs, Ideas to Impact, Walmart Vriddhi, conducted Session-I on Boosting MSMEs through E-Commerce and Export, highlighting digital marketplaces and digital enablement of small businesses. Shri Abhishek Rana, Associate CSR and Training, Meesho, conducted Session-II on the same theme, elaborating on opportunities for MSMEs to reach customers beyond geographical boundaries.
A key outcome was facilitation of e-commerce onboarding. 14 entrepreneurs were onboarded on Meesho, while 10 potential entrepreneurs were identified for onboarding with Walmart and Flipkart. The SLPMU team coordinated the onboarding process with participating agencies.

Union Health Minister Reviews Progress of Key Health Sector Projects Announced in Union Budget 2026-27
articles.full_content:
160 District Hospitals to be Strengthened in First Phase by March 2027; Focus on Expanding Emergency and Trauma Care Capacity Review focuses on strengthening drug regulation, expanding allied healthcare workforce, enhancing mental health and trauma care, and developing medical value tourism infrastructure
Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the progress of key projects and initiatives announced for the health sector in the Union Budget 2026-27 , with a focus on ensuring their timely implementation, effective inter-ministerial coordination and delivery of measurable outcomes. During the review, Shri Nadda took stock of the preparatory work undertaken by various departments of the Ministry and emphasised that Budget announcements should translate into concrete programmes, strengthened institutions and enhanced healthcare capacities within clearly defined timelines.
The Minister reviewed the progress of the initiative to increase emergency and trauma care capacity in District Hospitals by 50 per cent through establishment and strengthening of Emergency and Trauma Care Centres. He was informed that, following a post-Budget webinar, three committees were constituted to examine infrastructure, drugs, diagnostics and quality; human resources, academic expansion and skilling; and digital architecture and pre-hospital integration. A comprehensive gap analysis of District Hospitals against the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) has also been completed. Based on patient load, infrastructure and overall readiness, 613 District Hospitals have been categorised for phased implementation , with 160 District Hospitals identified for Phase I and targeted for strengthening by March 2027 . Phase II will cover 203 District Hospitals and Phase III the remaining 250. Shri Nadda stressed the need for close monitoring so that the first phase progresses in a focused and time-bound manner.
The Minister also reviewed the progress of National Emergency Life Support (NELS) training, aimed at strengthening the emergency care skills and competencies of healthcare professionals and frontline personnel. The training is envisaged to enhance preparedness for timely assessment, stabilisation and management of patients with life-threatening conditions, thereby complementing the expansion of emergency and trauma care capacity in District Hospitals.
The Minister also reviewed progress on the Budget initiative to strengthen the Allied Health Professionals (AHPs) ecosystem , with the objective of adding 1 lakh AHPs over the next five years across 10 selected disciplines. He was informed that consultations have been undertaken with industry, State Governments, Central and State Government institutions and hospitals, implementing agencies and regulatory bodies. Tribal Artisan Empanelment Mela held for PM Vishwakarma Artisans, Nagaland and NSRLM Artisans
articles.full_content:
A Tribal Artisan Empanelment Mela was jointly organized by TRIFED, the Ministry of MSME (Government of India), and the Directorate of Industries and Commerce (Government of Nagaland) on August 27, 2026. Held at the Directorate’s Conference Hall in Kohima, the event brought together PM Vishwakarma-trained artisans alongside participants from the Nagaland State Rural Livelihood Mission (NSRLM).
Tribal Artisan Empanelment Mela led by the Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED) under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs identifies, registers, and directly sources handcrafted products from indigenous artisans. Empaneled artisans gain access to TRIFED’s commercial network, including "Tribes India" retail outlets, national/international exhibitions (like Aadi Mahotsav), and integrated e-commerce platforms.
The event began with a welcome address from the State Programme Management Unit, PM Vishwakarma. This was followed by an address note from Shri Hojeto K Suqhe, Joint Director, Industries and Commerce. He highlighted that the Empanelment Mela is a strategic convergence between the Ministry of MSME and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. It leverages the core strengths of both programs combining supply-side capacity building with demand-side market access. Through TRIFED's empanelment mechanism, these skilled Naga artisans, particularly those in indigenous craft sectors like basketry, woodworking, and textiles, can directly plug into nationwide retail channels, ensuring sustainable livelihoods and global visibility for regional handicrafts.
An introductory session on TRIFED was conducted by Shri Asif Ekbal Hussain, Senior Program executive, TRIFED. He spoke on the objectives of TRIFED, the empanelment process and the importance of product-market fit in terms of quality and pricing. This was followed by the empanelment process where the TRIFED officials inspected the products showcased by the artisans. The products ranged from bamboo and cane baskets, crochet dolls, handloom products and local food items.
The mela resulted in an expression of interest by TRIFED for 28 products made by the artisans. These products would be examined by the committee at the TRIFED Regional office to determine product quality and feasibility for onboarding on TRIFED's market channels.

CSIR-SERC and SVCE Host Two-Day Structural Engineering Workshop Under CSIR-Integrated Skill Initiative
articles.full_content: CSIR-Structural Engineering Research Centre (CSIR-SERC), Chennai, in collaboration with Sri Venkateswara College of Engineering (SVCE), Sriperumbudur, organized a two-day workshop on "Structural Engineering" on August 24–25, 2026, under the national CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative aligned with Skill India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Inaugurating the event, Dr. (Smt.) N. Anandavalli, Director, CSIR-SERC, emphasized the necessity of bridging academic concepts with practical civil engineering solutions. Over the two days, senior CSIR-SERC scientists led sessions on diverse, cutting-edge topics: Dr. S. Maheswaran provided an overview of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), Dr. V. Srinivas discussed Structural Health Monitoring using bridge projects, Dr. P. Kamatchi introduced earthquake-resistant design fundamentals, Dr. Saptarshi Sasmal detailed nano/micro-scale self-sensing smart structures, Dr. S. Vishnuvardhan covered fatigue-resistant steel structures, and Dr. S. Sundar Kumar explained concrete design principles. Coordinated alongside Dr. R. Kumutha (HOD, Civil Engineering, SVCE) and department faculty, the workshop successfully exposed students to emerging technologies, real-world engineering applications, and IPR management.
